subject: Confidentiality & Brand consent: publicity notice, logo use, reference rights
messages:
From: Sara Ellis <sara.ellis@brighttech.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@brighttech.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightTech redlines on MSA - publicity and confidentiality

Marcus,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA. Our legal team reviewed the publicity and confidentiality sections and attached a marked-up version with BrightTech redlines. High-level concerns:

- Publicity: BrightTech cannot agree to a unilateral broad reference right or logo usage without an explicit opt-in process and a clear carveout for regulated product names.
- Press releases: we need a 15-business-day review for any joint press release and mutual approval on quotes.
- Confidentiality: the carveouts exclude information independently developed or already in the public domain, but the current language is ambiguous and could be interpreted to allow broad commercial disclosures.

We proposed specific edits in the attachment. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the mutual approval window and the limitation on logo use to an approved customer page only.

Attachment: BrightTech_Redlines_MSA_v2.docx (redline)

Sara Ellis

Subject: Re: BrightTech redlines on MSA - publicity and confidentiality

Thanks Sara — appreciate the thorough redline.

Kimberly / Priyom, looping you in to review the proposed edits on publicity and confidentiality. Key asks from BrightTech: 15 business days for release review, mutual approval on quotes, and a constrained logo consent (approved customer page only). They also flagged an ambiguous confidentiality carveout that could be read broadly.

My ask: can Legal propose clean fallback language that balances BrightTechs needs with our product marketing goals? Specifically, can we:
1) Limit logo usage to an approved customer reference page and marketing one-pagers, with an explicit opt-in and ability for customer to revoke.
2) Agree to a 10-15 business day review period for press releases, but with a fast-track option (3 business days) for product bug/incident reporting communications.
3) Tighten confidentiality carveouts so public domain and independently developed info remain excluded but require written proof where feasible.

Sara — if you have discretion on reducing the review window to 10 business days under certain conditions, let us know. Once Legal posts suggested language I will run it past our CS and Marketing teams.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Sara Ellis <sara.ellis@brighttech.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: BrightTech redlines on MSA - publicity and confidentiality

Marcus, Sara — thanks for the context. I reviewed BrightTechs redlines and drafted proposed language below and in an attached doc. I tried to keep the controls BrightTech wants while preserving reasonable marketing rights for Redwood. Summary of our proposed positions: 

1) Logo and reference rights
- Proposal: Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use Customer name and logo solely in Redwood marketing materials and on a Redwood customer reference page ("Approved Customer Page"). Any use outside those locations requires separate written consent. Customer may request removal with 30 days notice; Redwood will comply unless a previously agreed campaign is underway, in which case Redwood will remove at the next materially reasonable opportunity.

2) Press releases and quotes
- Proposal: Mutual review and approval for press releases referencing the relationship. Each party will respond to approval requests within 10 business days. For joint incident communications or legal notices, a 3 business day response is reasonable. Edits limited to factual corrections and trademark usage; substantive marketing changes require mutual written consent.

3) Confidentiality carveouts
- Clarification: Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes publicly known other than through a breach by the receiving party; (b) is independently developed by the receiving party; or (c) is rightfully obtained from a third party without restriction. Where a party seeks to rely on a carveout, it shall provide written evidence (redaction allowed) if the other party reasonably requests proof.

4) Reference quotes and case studies
- Proposal: Redwood may seek quotes for case studies; Customer will make a best reasonable effort to provide a quote within 10 business days. Customer approval on the final text is required prior to publication; minor grammatical edits may be made by Redwood with notice.

I attached a short doc with the exact redline language for insertion into the MSA. If BrightTech is firm on 15 business days, we can accept that for initial launch customers but would like 10 days as the standard.

Attachment: RDW_Suggested_Publicity_Language.docx

Kimberly and Marcus — thank you for the quick turnaround and the clear proposals. I reviewed the suggested language and the team is comfortable with the following with one small tweak: we will accept the 10 business day standard for press review provided that any request for confidential treatment of specific quote text must be submitted with the approval request and documented. We also need a specific call-out that logos used on third-party partner portals require additional consent.

We made the tweak in the attached acceptance note and asked our counsel to prepare a final redline. Once you send a final agreed redline we will have our GC sign off.
